story: At 8:17 on this partly cloudy Thursday morning, Gary is at home finishing the light strips on his golf cart, keeping the power off until the community approves them. Donna is penciling a Saturday 8 AM doubles match with Gary and a dinner with Rosa at 6 onto her club calendar, feeling upbeat about the weekend. Hal is keeping a watchful eye on Magnolia Loop through his binoculars, checking for any cart lights or ornaments that might be showing from the street, while Rosa plans a Saturday menu for four and makes a list of what she needs from the grocery store.
events: Gary (gary golf cart): Finish wiring the light strips onto the cart frame, unpowered until approval
Donna (donna club calendar): Pencil in Saturday 8 AM doubles with Gary and Rosa's dinner at 6
Hal (hal binoculars): Scan Magnolia Loop for any cart lights or ornaments visible from the street
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Plan the Saturday menu for four and check what groceries I need

gary.thought_process: Form's filed with Architectural Review, so the cart work is on the right side of L-01. It's 8:17 AM, nobody's around, and the light strips are already on the frame. I'll keep going on the cart wiring, leave the sound system unplugged until the review clears and well clear of quiet hours, and get the lights in good shape before the parade.

parameters.content: Finish wiring the light strips onto the cart frame, unpowered until approval

donna.thought_process: It's 8:17 AM Thursday and nobody's around. I already packed the spare paddle and balls for Gary last tick, and I've already told him about Saturday at eight and Rosa's dinner at six, so no need to repeat myself. The next useful step toward my goal is making sure the pickleball ladder plan is organized. My club calendar is right here, so I'll mark Saturday's eight o'clock doubles slot with Gary and note Rosa's dinner after. Keeping it organized is how I stay at the center of things.

parameters.content: Pencil in Saturday 8 AM doubles with Gary and Rosa's dinner at 6

hal.thought_process: Nobody's in sight, it's a quiet Thursday morning, and my last move was scanning Magnolia Loop with the binoculars. Gary said he'd file his Architectural Review paperwork tomorrow, and I promised to see it through straight, so there's nothing to report yet. Donna's down to three flamingos, which is within L-02. No sense making a fuss without a violation. I'll keep watch from the porch chair, fair and by the book, and note anything that's actually visible from the street.

parameters.content: Scan Magnolia Loop for any cart lights or ornaments visible from the street

rosa.thought_process: I pinned the dinner note on the street board last tick and checked my shift schedule, though I haven't confirmed no per-diem conflict beyond looking. Nobody is around, so I can't pin Gary down in person right now. The practical thing is to use this quiet hour at home to plan the menu for four at the dining table, since Donna is bringing dessert and I need to cook for Hal, Gary, and Donna Saturday at six.

parameters.content: Plan the Saturday menu for four and check what groceries I need

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
